title: Signature Router First-Run
body:
The Signature Router First-Run is Manon's original design for a ritual performed the day a router arrives, before any device depends on it. The ritual changes the admin password, sets a strong Wi-Fi password, turns on updates, and turns off remote admin access, in that order, with each step ticked on a card. Its premise is that the router is the home's front door, and front doors are locked before furniture is moved in.

The design exists because setup day is the only day the router is still a stranger to every device in the home.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: the home network is a place, not a pipe, so strangers are not admitted by default; every device must be removable without breaking the home; and a device that cannot be updated is a device with an expiry date, which the household must know.

The working method is Signature router first-run ritual. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Change the admin password from its factory value first
  2. Set a strong, unique Wi-Fi password second
  3. Turn on automatic updates third
  4. Turn off remote admin access fourth
  5. Store the new passwords away from the router and tick the card

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Admin password changed first; OK :: Wi-Fi password set second; OK :: Updates on third; OK :: Remote admin off fourth; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The ritual is a procedure, not a router tool, and router interfaces differ, so it teaches the order rather than menu paths. Where a router offers no update option, the ritual's last step is to note its age and plan replacement. A common mistake is connecting devices first and promising to secure the router later, a later that rarely arrives. title: Signature Guest-Wi-Fi Gate
body:
The Signature Guest-Wi-Fi Gate is Manon's original design for a gate between visitors and the trusted home network. Visitors receive only the guest password, the guest network cannot reach trusted devices, and the guest password changes after gatherings. Its premise is that hospitality and network trust are different gifts, and a home can offer the first generously while guarding the second.

The design treats a guest's phone as a guest's shoes: welcome in the house, not in every room.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: the home network is a place, not a pipe, so strangers are not admitted by default; every device must be removable without breaking the home; and a device that cannot be updated is a device with an expiry date, which the household must know.

The working method is Signature guest-network gate. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Create a guest network with its own password
  2. Verify the guest network cannot reach trusted devices
  3. Share only the guest password with visitors
  4. Change the guest password after large gatherings
  5. Switch the guest network off during long stretches without guests

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Guest network created; OK :: Guest isolation verified; OK :: Only guest password shared; OK :: Guest password changed after gatherings; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The gate is a configuration habit, not a guarantee, and on routers without a guest option its fallback is a separate access point or a main-password change after guests leave. It does not inspect visitors' devices. A common mistake is sharing the main password with a visitor to save a minute, and thereby admitting their device to the trusted network. title: Signature Listening-Room Switch
body:
The Signature Listening-Room Switch is Manon's original design for a discipline around speakers and cameras: every device gets a physical switch habit, a history habit, and a placement rule. The switch habit is testing mute and shutter controls; the history habit is opening recording history monthly; the placement rule is that no camera covers a bedroom, bathroom, or guest's private space. Its premise is that a device's privacy is the sum of its controls, not any single switch.

The design exists because a glowing mute light is a claim, and claims deserve checking.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: the home network is a place, not a pipe, so strangers are not admitted by default; every device must be removable without breaking the home; and a device that cannot be updated is a device with an expiry date, which the household must know.

The working method is Signature speaker-and-camera switch discipline. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Test the mute or shutter control on every speaker and camera
  2. Open recording history monthly and delete what is unneeded
  3. Set retention to the shortest useful period
  4. Agree openly who may review household recordings
  5. Place cameras by the placement rule, never by convenience alone

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Mute and shutter tested; OK :: History opened monthly; OK :: Retention set short; OK :: Placement rule followed; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The discipline is personal, not technical, and it cannot promise that any particular service keeps recordings secure. Households needing stronger assurance are directed by the design to prefer devices that work locally. A common mistake is trusting a mute light without ever opening the recording history it supposedly protects. title: Signature Factory-Key Reset
body:
The Signature Factory-Key Reset is Manon's original design for a sweep performed on setup day: every device's factory credential is changed, important devices get unique passwords, and the sweep is repeated whenever a device is reset. Its name says its premise plainly: a factory key is a key the factory gave everyone, so it is not a key at all until it is changed.

The design exists because the easiest entry into a home is the one printed in a manual.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: the home network is a place, not a pipe, so strangers are not admitted by default; every device must be removable without breaking the home; and a device that cannot be updated is a device with an expiry date, which the household must know.

The working method is Signature factory-credential reset sweep. Follow these steps in order:

  1. List every connected device on setup day
  2. Change each factory admin password
  3. Give cameras and locks unique passwords
  4. Store device passwords away from the devices themselves
  5. Repeat the sweep after any device reset

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Devices listed; OK :: Factory passwords changed; OK :: Cameras and locks unique; OK :: Sweep repeated after resets; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The sweep is a habit, not a tool, and some devices offer only one shared password or none. Where a device cannot be given its own password, the design moves it to the guest network and limits what it can reach. A common mistake is changing the Wi-Fi password while leaving each device's own factory password untouched. title: Signature Update Watcher
body:
The Signature Update Watcher is Manon's original design for a monthly routine: one person checks every device's update status, allows pending reboots, and notes which devices have stopped receiving updates. Its premise is that updates are the maker's ongoing care for a device, and a device whose care has stopped is a device with an expiry date the household must know.

The design treats an unchecked update status as an unanswered letter from the maker.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: the home network is a place, not a pipe, so strangers are not admitted by default; every device must be removable without breaking the home; and a device that cannot be updated is a device with an expiry date, which the household must know.

The working method is Signature update-status watcher routine. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Turn on automatic updates where offered
  2. Check update status for every device monthly
  3. Allow reboots that updates request
  4. Note devices that no longer receive updates
  5. Put the router first in every check, since all devices depend on it

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Automatic updates on; OK :: Status checked this month; OK :: Reboots allowed; OK :: Router checked first; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The watcher is a routine, not a patching tool, and updates can occasionally change a feature. Its monthly check is the balance: frequent enough to catch drift, calm enough to notice changes. A common mistake is assuming updates happen because they were once enabled, without ever checking. title: Signature Stranger-Device Bell
body:
The Signature Stranger-Device Bell is Manon's original design for a monthly bell: when it rings, someone opens the connected-device list and names every device aloud. A name nobody recognizes is treated as a bell that keeps ringing until it is explained, blocked, and followed by a password change. Its premise is that intrusions are usually discovered by a person noticing a name, not by an alarm.

The design gives the household a ritual for the review, because reviews without a ritual are forgotten.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: the home network is a place, not a pipe, so strangers are not admitted by default; every device must be removable without breaking the home; and a device that cannot be updated is a device with an expiry date, which the household must know.

The working method is Signature connected-device review bell. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Open the connected-device list when the bell rings
  2. Name each device and match it to a household member or guest
  3. Rename known devices clearly for future reviews
  4. Block unrecognized devices and change the Wi-Fi password
  5. Ring the bell monthly and after every gathering

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Device list opened on the bell; OK :: Every device named and matched; OK :: Known devices renamed; OK :: Unknown device blocked; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The bell is a ritual, not a monitor, and device names can be changed by their owners, so a name never proves safety. Its value is catching persistent strangers, not guaranteeing a clean network. A common mistake is dismissing an unknown device because the network still works. title: Signature Door-and-Bell Guard
body:
The Signature Door-and-Bell Guard is Manon's original design for entrance devices: one code per person, codes removed when access ends, a physical key kept as backup, and recording retention kept short. Its premise is that a shared code is a copied key that cannot be taken back, so the design refuses shared codes entirely.

The design exists because convenience at the door is paid for in access that cannot be revoked cleanly.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: the home network is a place, not a pipe, so strangers are not admitted by default; every device must be removable without breaking the home; and a device that cannot be updated is a device with an expiry date, which the household must know.

The working method is Signature lock-and-doorbell guard. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Issue one entry code per person, never a shared code
  2. Remove codes promptly when access ends
  3. Keep a physical key for power and network failures
  4. Set doorbell recording retention short and review viewers
  5. Test lock behavior during power and network outages

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: One code per person; OK :: Stale codes removed; OK :: Physical key kept; OK :: Failure behavior tested; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The guard is a practice, not a lock, and it cannot promise any lock works in every failure mode. Households must test their own lock and keep a physical backup, and the design does not cover recording law. A common mistake is sharing one code with helpers and never changing it when help ends. title: Signature Nursery Camera Code
body:
The Signature Nursery Camera Code is Manon's original design for the strictest code in the home, governing cameras in children's rooms. The code requires unique passwords, monthly update checks, covering when not in use, viewing limited to named household members, and placement agreed openly. Its premise is that a camera watching a vulnerable person deserves more rules, not fewer, than any other device.

The design treats a child's room as a sanctuary, and a camera there as a guest that must earn its place.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: the home network is a place, not a pipe, so strangers are not admitted by default; every device must be removable without breaking the home; and a device that cannot be updated is a device with an expiry date, which the household must know.

The working method is Signature monitor-and-camera code. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Give the monitor a unique password, never its factory value
  2. Check its software monthly
  3. Cover or switch off the camera when not actively needed
  4. Limit viewing to named household members
  5. Agree placement openly with everyone in the household

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Unique password set; OK :: Software checked monthly; OK :: Camera covered when idle; OK :: Viewing limited to named members; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The code is a discipline, not a promise about any service's security, and images that leave the home to a service are beyond the household's direct control. The design prefers cameras that work locally where stronger assurance is needed. A common mistake is leaving a monitor on its factory password because setup was difficult the first time. title: Signature Screen Privacy Dial
body:
The Signature Screen Privacy Dial is Manon's original design for a dial, turned deliberately, that sets how much a television and its apps may learn. The dial's positions are: viewing-data collection off where offered, app permissions reviewed, personal apps signed out before guests, and a repeat review after major updates. Its premise is that a television watches back in data, so its privacy must be set, not assumed.

The design exists because nobody opens a television's privacy settings by accident.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: the home network is a place, not a pipe, so strangers are not admitted by default; every device must be removable without breaking the home; and a device that cannot be updated is a device with an expiry date, which the household must know.

The working method is Signature TV-and-streaming privacy dial. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Open the TV's privacy settings and read each choice
  2. Turn viewing-data collection off where offered
  3. Review each streaming app's permissions
  4. Sign out of personal apps before guests use the TV
  5. Repeat the review after major software updates

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. title: Signature Voice Data Vault
body:
The Signature Voice Data Vault is Manon's original design for treating voice history as a vault whose contents are reviewed, pruned, and guarded. The vault's rules are: open the history monthly, delete what is unneeded, set retention short, agree openly who may review it, and mute in rooms where private conversation happens. Its premise is that voice captures background as well as commands, so its keeping deserves a decision.

The design treats a voice recording as a letter that was never meant to be kept forever.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: the home network is a place, not a pipe, so strangers are not admitted by default; every device must be removable without breaking the home; and a device that cannot be updated is a device with an expiry date, which the household must know.

The working method is Signature voice-history vault discipline. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Open voice history monthly
  2. Delete unneeded recordings, individually or in bulk
  3. Set retention to the shortest useful period
  4. Agree openly who may review the vault
  5. Use mute in rooms where private conversation happens

title: Signature Device Neighborhoods
body:
The Signature Device Neighborhoods is Manon's original design for dividing the home network into neighborhoods: trusted computers and phones in one, home devices in another, guests in a third. Home devices may reach the internet but not the trusted neighborhood, so a compromised camera cannot walk into private files. Its premise is that a network, like a town, is safer with neighborhoods than with one open square.

The design exists because one weak gadget should not expose every file in the home.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: the home network is a place, not a pipe, so strangers are not admitted by default; every device must be removable without breaking the home; and a device that cannot be updated is a device with an expiry date, which the household must know.

The working method is Signature network segmentation neighborhoods. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Sort devices into trusted, home-device, and guest neighborhoods
  2. Place home devices in their own neighborhood where the router allows
  3. Verify the home-device neighborhood cannot reach trusted computers
  4. Place guests in the guest neighborhood only
  5. Re-sort whenever a new device joins the home

The design applies whatever split the equipment allows and does not promise any particular feature. A common mistake is putting every device in one neighborhood because sorting sounds complicated. title: Signature Firmware Health Check
body:
The Signature Firmware Health Check is Manon's original design for a twice-yearly health check: firmware version, update status, and the maker's support statement for every device. A device past support is moved to the guest neighborhood or disconnected, and its replacement is planned and budgeted. Its premise is that devices do not announce their own expiry, so the household must ask.

The design treats support as a device's lifeblood: when it stops, the device is living on borrowed time.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: the home network is a place, not a pipe, so strangers are not admitted by default; every device must be removable without breaking the home; and a device that cannot be updated is a device with an expiry date, which the household must know.

The working method is Signature firmware-and-support health check. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Check firmware and update status twice a year
  2. Find each maker's support statement
  3. Move past-support devices off the trusted network
  4. Plan and budget replacements
  5. Record support end dates on the household device list

Its fallback, moving a device to the guest neighborhood, is the protection when certainty is unavailable. A common mistake is keeping a past-support camera on the trusted network because it still works perfectly. title: Signature Office-Home Divider
body:
The Signature Office-Home Divider is Manon's original design for a line between work and home on the same wire: a work segment or Wi-Fi name, a work device nobody else uses, and a rule that work material never travels to personal devices. Its premise is that two worlds sharing one network share each other's risks, and a line drawn deliberately is cheaper than a breach shared accidentally.

The design exists because work from home blends worlds, and blends are where risks meet.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: the home network is a place, not a pipe, so strangers are not admitted by default; every device must be removable without breaking the home; and a device that cannot be updated is a device with an expiry date, which the household must know.

The working method is Signature home-office divider. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Create a work segment or Wi-Fi name where possible
  2. Reserve a work device for work only
  3. Never move work material to personal devices
  4. Follow employer device and network rules where they exist
  5. Review the divider whenever the home network changes

title: Signature Clean-Handover Ritual
body:
The Signature Clean-Handover Ritual is Manon's original design for a ritual performed before any device leaves the household: sign out of every account, remove the device from trusted lists, factory reset, verify the setup screen, and wipe removable storage. Its order matters, because a reset before sign-out can leave the device tied to the old account. Its premise is that a handed-over device is a handed-over diary unless the ritual is followed.

The design treats order as the protection, since most failed handovers fail on order, not on effort.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: the home network is a place, not a pipe, so strangers are not admitted by default; every device must be removable without breaking the home; and a device that cannot be updated is a device with an expiry date, which the household must know.

The working method is Signature device handover ritual. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Sign out of every account before resetting
  2. Remove the device from trusted-device lists
  3. Factory reset and verify the setup screen appears
  4. Wipe or remove removable storage
  5. Change the Wi-Fi password if a stranger now holds a device that knew it

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Accounts signed out first; OK :: Trusted lists cleaned; OK :: Setup screen verified; OK :: Storage wiped; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The ritual is a procedure, not a promise of complete erasure, since some older storage retains data past a reset. For highly sensitive devices, the design's stronger answer is physical destruction of storage. A common mistake is resetting without signing out first, leaving the device tied to the old account. title: Signature Whole-Home Audit Wheel
body:
The Signature Whole-Home Audit Wheel is Manon's original design for a wheel that turns once a year: router, passwords, updates, connected devices, camera placement, and the device list, each a spoke checked in one sitting. Its premise is that home safety decays by drift, and only a scheduled wheel notices drift, because drift announces nothing.

The design gives the audit a wheel and a date, because audits without a date are intentions, not events.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: the home network is a place, not a pipe, so strangers are not admitted by default; every device must be removable without breaking the home; and a device that cannot be updated is a device with an expiry date, which the household must know.

The working method is Signature annual audit wheel. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Walk the router spoke: admin password, updates, remote access
  2. Walk the password spoke: Wi-Fi, devices, guest network
  3. Walk the update and support spoke for every device
  4. Walk the device and camera spoke: list and placement
  5. Update the device list and set next year's wheel date

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Router spoke walked; OK :: Password spoke walked; OK :: Update spoke walked; OK :: Device and camera spoke walked; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The wheel is a snapshot, and a device added the week after escapes notice until the next turn. The design therefore pairs the annual wheel with the monthly stranger-device bell. A common mistake is checking only the router and calling the home done. title: Signature Shared-Home Device Charter
body:
The Signature Shared-Home Device Charter is Manon's original design for a charter agreed openly in rented and shared homes: who controls the router, which shared devices exist, who may view their recordings, and what happens on moving out. Its premise is that a shared home's devices are shared witnesses, and sharing must be agreed, not discovered.

The design exists because a device in your room that belongs to someone else is not your device.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: the home network is a place, not a pipe, so strangers are not admitted by default; every device must be removable without breaking the home; and a device that cannot be updated is a device with an expiry date, which the household must know.

The working method is Signature shared-home device charter. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Ask who controls the router and what it records
  2. Agree openly which shared devices exist and who views them
  3. Keep personal accounts off shared devices where possible
  4. Use a personal segment or hotspot for sensitive personal use
  5. Remove personal accounts from shared devices before moving out
